sources.name: BANKING77
sources.real_or_synthetic: human-authored queries; not customer-support conversation logs
sources.provenance_notes: Published by PolyAI in its official task-specific-datasets repository and associated with the ACL 2020 paper Efficient Intent Detection with Dual Sentence Encoders.
sources.privacy_notes: The official source describes annotated online-banking queries, not released bank call logs or production transcripts. Treat utterances as public benchmark text and preserve attribution.
sources.intended_use: The test split is a consumed historical external intent-generalization benchmark. Under the later V2-C3 decision, only train.csv may contribute to conditional development and fresh-lockbox allocation under the frozen registry restrictions.

sources.name: CFPB Consumer Complaint Database Narratives Archive
sources.dataset_type: archived consumer-written financial complaint narratives and complaint metadata
sources.real_or_synthetic: publicly released, consumer-authored real complaint narratives; not support conversations or application customer records
sources.language: Primarily English; language coverage requires inspection before use
sources.approximate_size: Archive of previously published narratives received from 2011-12-01 through 2026-08-14; record count not qualified in this phase
sources.label_structure: Complaint product, sub-product, issue, sub-issue, company, response, and related metadata; no clean SentinelVoice intent labels
sources.license: The CFPB states that published complaint data is freely available to use, analyze, and build on, and that previously published narratives are in the public domain for FOIA purposes. Use and redistribution terms still require review before acquisition; this is not represented as a conventional ML-dataset license.
sources.provenance_notes: Official CFPB FOIA Reading Room archive of public consumer-authored complaints previously published in the Consumer Complaint Database, covering complaints received from 2011-12-01 through 2026-08-14.
sources.privacy_notes: Public narratives required consumer opt-in publication consent and CFPB personal-information scrubbing intended to minimize, not eliminate, re-identification risk. SentinelVoice must perform additional privacy and sensitive-content review and must not intentionally retain credentials, account secrets, or PII.
limitations: Narratives are one-sided consumer allegations and were not independently verified by the CFPB complaint process.
The complaints are not a representative sample of consumers or financial-market experiences.
SentinelVoice must not use complaint narratives or volumes to rank or judge financial institutions.
Public release and scrubbing do not make the free-form narratives perfectly anonymized or risk-free.
sources.intended_use: Offline language robustness, intent, ambiguity, long-form, multi-intent, and out-of-distribution evaluation only; not automatic intent-label training and never application customer/account data.

sources.name: Bitext Retail Banking Tagged Training Dataset for LLM-based Virtual Assistants
sources.dataset_type: tagged retail-banking intent and question-answer corpus
sources.real_or_synthetic: hybrid synthetic; generated with Bitext NLP/NLG technology and automated labeling tools
sources.label_structure: 26 intents in 9 categories, with instruction, response, entity placeholders, and language-generation tags
sources.provenance_notes: The publisher-controlled dataset card explicitly describes the source as hybrid synthetic and documents its automated generation and labeling process.
sources.privacy_notes: Synthetic templates include entity placeholders rather than verified production customer records. It must not be described as real-world bank conversation data.
sources.intended_use: Secondary cross-source benchmark or candidate for a separately approved later augmentation study; not the primary real-language benchmark.

sources.name: CLINC150 / OOS Evaluation Dataset
sources.dataset_type: general-domain intent classification with explicit out-of-scope examples
sources.real_or_synthetic: crowdsourced scenario responses and paraphrases; not production conversation logs
sources.approximate_size: 23,700 examples in the full configuration: 22,500 in-scope and 1,200 out-of-scope
sources.label_structure: 150 single-intent in-scope classes with 100 train, 20 validation, and 30 test examples per class; OOS has 100 train, 100 validation, and 1,000 test examples
sources.provenance_notes: Official repository accompanying the EMNLP 2019 paper An Evaluation Dataset for Intent Classification and Out-of-Scope Prediction. The creators state that examples were crowdsourced and are single-intent.
sources.privacy_notes: Crowdsourced benchmark utterances are not authenticated customer interactions or bank support transcripts.
sources.intended_use: The test and processed evaluation splits remain historical external benchmarks. Under the later V2-C3 decision, only qualifying finance-domain train/val examples may contribute to conditional development and fresh-lockbox allocation; generic OOS examples remain excluded.

sources.name: Bank of America customer-support transcripts
sources.provenance_notes: No official publicly released de-identified customer-support conversation-log dataset was verified during V2-C2A. No unofficial mirror is accepted as a substitute.
sources.privacy_notes: Any future candidate would require official provenance, documented de-identification, consent or disclosure authority, and privacy review.
sources.intended_use: None unless an official source and license are verified in a later qualification review.

policy_history.decision: All external sources remained evaluation-only pending a separate training-governance decision.
Approved only BANKING77 train and qualifying CLINC finance train/val examples under the V2-C3 registry; CFPB, Bitext, unverified transcripts, and every consumed evaluation split remain prohibited.
